memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: "'Place the gold altar of incense in front of the ark of the covenant law and put the curtain at the entrance to the tabernacle. Place the altar of burnt offering in front of the entrance to the tabernacle, the tent of meeting; place the basin between the tent of meeting and the altar and put water in it.'" - Exod 40:5-7 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
Three items, and their placement tells a story.

The altar of incense stood closest to God's presence — prayer belongs nearest the throne. The altar of burnt offering stood outside at the entrance — sacrifice comes first for anyone approaching. And between them, the basin of water for washing.

Read from the outside in, that is a map of coming to God. Sacrifice. Cleansing. Then prayer in His presence.

This is not a formula we must climb. It is the shape of what Christ has already accomplished. He offered Himself once for all as the sacrifice (Heb 10:10). We are washed by the water of the word and cleansed by His blood (Eph 5:26; 1 John 1:7). And because both are done, we come near to pray with confidence (Heb 4:16).

Notice the basin sat between the altar and the tent. Cleansing was not a one-time event for the priests; they washed repeatedly as they served (Exod 30:19-21). Our standing before God is settled once, but our daily walk needs regular washing — which is why John writes that if we confess our sins, He is faithful and just to forgive and purify us (1 John 1:9).

Justified once. Cleansed daily.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. Do you approach God through Christ's sacrifice or your own worthiness?
2. Is confession a regular part of your walk, or only for emergencies?
3. Where does prayer sit in your daily priorities?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Lord, thank You that the sacrifice is made and the washing provided. Keep me coming to You cleansed and confident. Amen.
